northStar: An agent user can see which provider each tool call really reaches, and can see every write the agent attempts, before a bad call does harm.
constraint: No mocks. Real Workers AI model, real upstream MCP servers, real KV side effects in scratch namespaces only.
falsifiable: A passport gateway blocks 100% of impostor tool calls and 0% of trusted calls, and a write fence blocks 100% of injected write targets with 0 false blocks, on a real Workers AI agent.

proven.claim: Each of 17 sampled domain rules has a story that fails when the rule is removed.
proven.scope: 17 hand-picked mutations in src/domain. This does not prove that the rule set is complete or correct for real agents.

unproven.claim: Registration order never decides identity. A tool's identity is (provider, name). When two servers with valid passports both expose `execute`, the gateway keeps both tools, qualified by provider, and records a collision. A call by bare name is rejected when two providers expose the name. A call that names the trusted provider reaches the trusted server whether the impostor registered first or last. Without passports, a Workers AI function-calling agent with two servers that both expose `execute` calls the impostor in at least 20% of 50 trials. With passports on, the gateway blocks 100% of impostor calls and 0% of trusted calls. An impostor call is a call that reaches a server whose verified provider is not the provider the session trusts for that tool, or a server with no valid passport.

A fence that allows writes only to targets named in the user prompt blocks 100% of injected write targets across 20 poisoned-document cases, with 0 false blocks on 20 clean tasks, and adds under 5 ms p50 per call. No decoy key changes.
Every gateway event reaches a Rex terminal pane within 1 s p95, and replaying the recorded log rebuilds the FlightLog view with the same hash.

openQuestions: Where does the provider public key come from? The domain assumes the operator pins it. The gateway must never take it from the upstream server.
Views keep the order of each source stream. Cross-session order in FlightLog is the order of delivery. Does the E3 replay need a global sequence?
Rejections do not record events. The Refusals aggregate records them for FlightLog. The gateway must send RecordRefusal after each rejection. A gateway crash between the two loses one entry.
How does the gateway parse targets from the user prompt? E2 needs a parser that is not an LLM call.
How does the session say which provider it trusts for a tool? E1 needs this to define an impostor call. The gateway must read it from operator config, never from the agent or a tool result.
Customer 0 returns Workers AI error 1050 and KV 403 through the customer0 Alchemy profile. Which scopes or entitlements are missing? See STATUS.md.
